note: No hosting server. A did:webs DID is hosted only — the VTA has no inbound surface to serve one from — so there is no serverless form, and a request without `serverId` must fail validation rather than fall back to one.

The path carries the AID. The caller cannot know the AID — it is the digest of an inception event the VTA has not yet written — and the slot grammar is lowercase, so a case-sensitive AID segment is refused rather than taken as a path the VTA then appends a second AID to.
A path with a leading slash. The slot grammar has no empty segment, so `/people` would publish a DID with an empty label.
Caller-supplied key material. The VTA derives every key; a request naming a signing key is a request to custody a key the caller chose, and the closed schema refuses it.
An alias that is not a DID. Designated aliases are DIDs; a URL here would be published as one.
A service without an endpoint. A designated service is rendered into the document as given, and one with no `serviceEndpoint` is not a service.
A service id that is not a fragment. Ids are relative to the DID; an absolute id could name another DID's service.
A response without the committed successor. Every live did:webs DID this family creates commits one (nt 1); a response that omits it hides whether pre-rotation is in place.
